slot.brief: Two capacitors (charged and uncharged, or at different voltages) connected in parallel; find charge redistributed and fraction of stored energy lost.

stem: A $2\ \mu$F capacitor charged to $12$ V is connected in parallel, with like plates together, to an uncharged $4\ \mu$F capacitor. Find the charge transferred to the uncharged capacitor and the fraction of the initial energy lost.

verdicts.working: Initial charge is 2×12 = 24 μC. The final common voltage is 24/(2+4) = 4 V, so the 4 μF capacitor receives 4×4 = 16 μC. Initial and final energies are 144 μJ and 48 μJ, respectively; the fraction lost is (144−48)/144 = 2/3.

working:
Initial charge: $Q=2\times12=24\ \mu$C; final voltage: $V_f=24/(2+4)=4$ V.
Charge on initially uncharged capacitor: $q=4\times4=16\ \mu$C.
$U_i=\dfrac12(2)(12^2)=144\ \mu$J; $U_f=\dfrac12(6)(4^2)=48\ \mu$J.
Fraction lost $=\dfrac{144-48}{144}=\dfrac23$.

Independent check: Initial charge is 2×12 = 24 μC. The final common voltage is 24/(2+4) = 4 V, so the 4 μF capacitor receives 4×4 = 16 μC. Initial and final energies are 144 μJ and 48 μJ, respectively; the fraction lost is (144−48)/144 = 2/3.
solution:
Charge is conserved, so the common final voltage is $V_f=\dfrac{(2)(12)}{2+4}=4\text{ V}$. Hence the charge on the $4\,\mu\text{F}$ capacitor is $q=(4)(4)=16\,\mu\text{C}$.
Initial and final energies are $U_i=\dfrac12(2)(12^2)=144\,\mu\text{J}$ and $U_f=\dfrac12(6)(4^2)=48\,\mu\text{J}$.
Thus the fraction of energy lost is $\dfrac{U_i-U_f}{U_i}=\dfrac{144-48}{144}=\dfrac23$.
